scenario_description:
Objective: Avoid relying on a nonfunctioning carbon-monoxide monitor during a cold, powerless night aboard.
Emerging Need: A general safety-stock notice is only background until an overnight plan, confirmed shore-power outage, and short pickup option align.
Decision Context: Observable records establish the outage, heater context, pickup window, and helper availability; the stored safety note identifies the AC-only monitor, lack of battery backup, preferred unpaid hold route, and cockpit drop-off limit.
Consequence: Timely attention can preserve a workable warning layer before boarding; after Friday pickup and helper access close, the same preparation cannot protect that night.

parameter.subject: Winter cabin-safety stock notice
parameter.body: Battery-powered marine carbon-monoxide alarms and other winter cabin-safety items are in stock this week. Unpaid counter holds for Friday pickup must be requested before 16:00 on February 13.

parameter.title: Overnight aboard during cabin varnish cure
parameter.description: Stay aboard to keep the companionway cracked while the aft trim cures; use the propane bulkhead heater if the cabin gets cold and no errands after boarding.

parameter.subject: B-dock shore power outage starts 17:00 today
parameter.body: Electrical work on B-dock is now confirmed for 17:00-22:00 today. Tenants staying aboard should plan for no shore power during that window and should use any non-electric heat only with a working carbon-monoxide alarm and ventilation.

parameter.content: I’m near Tacoma Chandlery until about 15:25, then on the ferry with spotty service. I can leave a small sealed item in the cockpit dry bag before 16:00 if you already know what to have them set aside.

parameter.subject: Friday pickup counter closed for weather
parameter.body: Due to the waterfront wind advisory, the pickup counter has closed for the day. Hold requests received after 16:00 will be processed Saturday at noon, and no walk-in safety-gear pickups are available tonight.
